transient_split.keywords: transient tonal split attack body tail drums separate routing parallel reverb saturation
slider_desc: Balance: both parts on channels 1/2, each with its own level. Split: the transients on 1/2 and the tonal part on 3/4, for processing them apart.
Level of the transient part (the attack of each hit).
Level of the tonal part (the body and the tail).
How easily a sound counts as a transient.
How long the transient part lasts after each onset.
Output level.
uses: More or less attack on drums without EQ
Turning down room and tail on a drum recording
Reverb or saturation on only the body or only the attack (Split mode)
Softening plucks and clicks
transient_split.properties: Input → fast (1 ms) and slow (25 ms) linked peak envelopes, 100 ms release → transient weight (fast − slow) / fast × Sensitivity, instant rise, fall over Decay → transient = x·w, tonal = x·(1 − w) → Balance: levels and sum on 1/2; Split: transient on 1/2, tonal on 3/4 → Output. No frequency bands, zero latency; the two parts always sum to the input.

The note value of the step when synced.
How much quieter each echo is than the one before.
How far the echoes are panned left and right in turn.

Low-pass on the echoes.

multi_tap_delay.properties: Input → 4 s stereo line → up to 8 taps at pattern × step (Time or a synced note), level (1 − Decay)^(k−1), alternating pan by Spread → sum → 12 dB/oct low cut and high cut → Dry/Wet Mix; the last tap feeds back. Zero latency.

Shortest time between two hits (stops double triggers).

Low-pass on the detector, to keep cymbals out.

drum_trigger.properties: Input (passes through) → mono sum → 12 dB/oct detector high-pass and low-pass → peak follower (5 ms release) → trigger (Threshold, Retrigger, 3 dB hysteresis) → 2 ms velocity window → note-on, note-off after Note Length. Incoming MIDI passes through at its own sample. About 2 ms from onset to note-on.

The frequency of the high peak.
High peak boost (up to +18 dB).
Width of the high peak: 0 is sharp, 10 is broad.
The frequency of the high shelf cut.

Output level.

Air and presence on vocals
Broad tone shaping on the mix bus or master

passive_eq.properties: Input → low shelf boost at 1.2 × Low Freq → low shelf cut at 2.2 × Low Freq → high peak at High Freq (Q from Bandwidth) → high shelf cut at Atten Freq (each skipped at 0) → tube stage (asymmetric tanh, 10 Hz DC blocker, skipped at 0%) → Output. Zero latency; every control at 0 leaves the sound untouched.

pitch_to_midi.card_desc: Audio to MIDI for Monophonic Lines
pitch_to_midi.keywords: midi pitch to midi audio to midi convert tracker detection yin monophonic bass vocal guitar melody note pitch bend transcribe
slider_desc: Level the line must reach to make a note (and 3 dB under it to end one).
Lowest note it looks for.
Highest note it looks for.
How long a pitch must hold before a note starts or ends (longer is steadier, shorter is faster).
Fixed gives every note Fixed Velocity; Level maps Threshold..0 dBFS to 1..127.
The velocity when Velocity is Fixed.
Moves the notes it sends.
On follows the pitch inside the note with pitch bend (range +/-2 semitones).
MIDI channel of the notes.
uses: Doubling a bass guitar with a synth bass
Turning a hummed or sung idea into MIDI
Layering a lead line with an instrument
Writing down a melody from a recording
pitch_to_midi.properties: Input (passes through) → mono sum → 30 Hz high-pass → 24 dB/oct low-pass → decimation to about 11 kHz → YIN pitch detection every 64 kept samples (threshold 0.15, parabolic interpolation) and window RMS → note state (Stability, 0.8 semitone hold, silence 3 dB under Threshold) → note-on, note-off, optional pitch bend. Monophonic. Latency about the window plus Stability (some tens of ms). Incoming MIDI passes through at its own sample.

note_echo.properties: MIDI in → every note-on adds Repeats echoes to a time-sorted queue (velocity x (1 - Decay)^k, pitch + k x Pitch Step, Gate of the interval) → notes out; a note that starts again while it sounds is ended first. Other MIDI passes through at its own sample; all notes off drops that channel's echoes. Audio passes through.
